rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the angels intercede only for those God approves, rulers should not trust their wealth or power, and subjects should fear the King of kings more than earthly kings.
rows.anchor: فيا أيها الملوك لا تغتروا بمالكم من المال والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike human rulers, God loses nothing by giving; the more children He grants, the more people fall under His rule and obligations, so abundant giving widens His dominion.
rows.anchor: أما الحق سبحانه وتعالى فملكه لا ينتقص بالعطاء والإحسان بل يزداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine kingship is complete only with mercy: 59:22 names God the Merciful before 59:23 calls Him King, Holy, Peace, and the giver of security from injustice.
rows.anchor: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب والشهادة هو الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of the King on that day with the Merciful means His kingship shows overwhelming power while His mercy removes fear and brings compassion.
rows.anchor: لما أثبت لنفسه الملك أردفه بان وصف نفسه بكونه رحمانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to seek refuge names God first as Lord of humanity and then as its King, showing kingship is perfected by care and mercy.
rows.anchor: فذكر أولا كونه ربا للناس ثم أردفه بكونه ملكا للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since disobedience to earthly kings can disorder society, people should obey their rulers and rulers should obey God; disbelief destroys the world, while prayer and piety bring its welfare.
rows.anchor: فإن خالفوه ولم يطيعوه وقع الهرج والمرج في العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's kingship on Judgment Day is displayed through justice and balanced scales; a human ruler is truly king only when just, while tyranny removes goodness from the world.
rows.anchor: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Anūshirwān story, a boy says fruit worsened when the king contemplated injustice and improved when he repented; the king then abandons tyranny, illustrating justice's worldly effects.
rows.anchor: لعل ملك البلد عزم على الظلم فلأجل شؤم ظلمه صار الرمان هكذا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī recommends Mālik (Owner) over Malik (King) because an owner suggests the servant may seek food, clothing, mercy, care, reward, and Paradise from him.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي : اقرأ مالك يوم الدين ؛ لأن هذه القراءة هي الدالة على الفضل الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant hopes in an owner for pardon, forgiveness, and Paradise as pure grace, whereas a king chiefly promises justice and equal treatment; this makes Mālik the more hopeful reading.
rows.anchor: والمالك أنت تطمع فيه وليست لنا طاعات ولا خيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An owner cares for an ill or weak servant and rescues him from distress, unlike a king who rejects an unfit soldier; Mālik therefore better suits sinners and the poor.
rows.anchor: أما المالك إذا كان له عبد فإن مرض عالجه وإن ضعف أعانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People need compassion and mercy more urgently than the awe and political force suggested by kingship, another reason Mālik is fitting.
rows.anchor: الملك له هيبة وسياسة والمالك له رأفة ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns existing things by being able to move them from existence to nonexistence or from one attribute to another; that power belongs only to Him.
rows.anchor: قادر على نقلها من الوجود إلى العدم أو بمعنى أنه قادر على نقلها من صفة إلى صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns the Day of Judgment because resurrection requires knowledge of every scattered bodily part and power over every possible thing.
rows.anchor: إذا كان الحشر والنشر والبعث والقيامة لا يتأتى إلا بعلم متعلق بجميع المعلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says a thing must already exist for its owner to own it, so the future Resurrection cannot yet be called God's possession; the contrast between قاتل زيد and قاتل زيدا illustrates the objection.
rows.anchor: القيامة غير موجودة في الحال فلا يكون الله مالكا ليوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that the Resurrection is so certain that wisdom treats it as already present, and every person who dies has already undergone his own resurrection.
rows.anchor: إلا أن قيام القيامة لما كان أمرا حقا لا يجوز الإخلال في الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five names span human time: God creates, nurtures, covers sins, forgives repentance, and finally delivers recompense as Owner of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: خلقتك أولا فأنا إله ثم ربيتك بوجوه النعم فأنا رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the merciful names emphasizes mercy more than other attributes, then the name Owner of Judgment Day prevents complacency; 40:3 similarly joins forgiveness and acceptance of repentance with stern punishment.
rows.anchor: اذكر أني رحمن رحيم مرتين لتعلم أن العناية بالرحمة أكثر منها بسائر الأمور

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: The Qadariyya argue that if God creates human deeds, reward for deeds people did not perform is pointless and punishment is unjust, undermining His ownership of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قالت القدرية : إن كان خالق أعمال العباد هو الله امتنع القول بالثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: الجبرية
rows.claim: The Jabriyya argue that unless God determines human deeds, He would not own them; since Muslims agree He owns people and their deeds, they infer He creates and determines them.
rows.anchor: وقالت الجبرية : لو لم تكن أعمال العباد بتقدير الله وترجيحه لم يكن مالكا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding anecdote is followed by a saying attributed to the Prophet: he was born during the reign of a just king, linking just rule with enduring renown.
rows.anchor: ولدت في زمن الملك العادل

none: Bare chapter heading introducing the explanation of 1:5.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is an act performed to magnify another; the word is related to a well-trodden, level road, طريق معبد.
rows.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن الفعل الذي يؤتى به لغرض تعظيم الغير وهو مأخوذ من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves worship because ultimate reverence belongs only to the source of greatest benefaction: life and the creation of what sustains life, both traced to God.
rows.anchor: الحياة التي تفيد المكنة من الانتفاع وخلق المنتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī's second proof begins by mapping God's names to the servant's past: God brought him from nonexistence, death, incapacity, and ignorance into being, life, ability, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: انتقل من العدم إلى الوجود ومن الموت إلى الحياة ومن العجز إلى القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant's needs multiply upon entering existence, setting up the claim that present provision depends on God as Lord, Merciful, and Compassionate.
rows.anchor: لما دخل في الوجوه انفتحت عليه أبواب الحاجات وحصلت عنده أسباب الضرورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's names cover all three stages of the servant's life: deity for his origin, Lord and the two Merciful names for present needs, and Owner of Judgment Day for the afterlife; all welfare depends on Him alone.
rows.anchor: جميع مصالح العبد في الماضي والحاضر والمستقبل لا يتم ولا يكتمل إلا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because divine power, knowledge, generosity, and forbearance are certain while natural, astral, or mental causes may also be effects of God's power, only God is certainly worthy of worship.
rows.anchor: العلم بكون الإله تعالى معبودا للخلق أمر يقيني وأما كون غيره معبودا للخلق فهو أمر مشكوك فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although servitude is lowly, service to the highest and most excellent Lord is most fitting; God's superior power, knowledge, and generosity make His worship preferable to any rival's.
rows.anchor: لما كان الله تعالى أشرف الموجودات وأعلاها فكانت عبوديته أولى من عبودية غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything contingent is needy and occupied with its own needs, so only the self-sufficient God can meet the needs of others and deserves their worship.
rows.anchor: والغني لذاته هو الله تعالى فدافع الحاجات هو الله تعالى فمستحق العبادات هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's extraordinary acts—holding the sky, moving celestial bodies, producing lightning, wind and rain, bringing water from stone and ice from water, and raising or lowering mountains and people—show why no created thing can share His worship.
rows.anchor: استحقاق العبادة يستدعي قدرة الله تعالى بأن يمسك سماء بلا علاقة وأرضا بلا دعامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's miracles, including raising the mountain over Moses and splitting the sea, make it foolish to equate Him in worship with inert, base, or finite creatures.
rows.anchor: وجعل البحر يبسا لموسى عليه السلام فمن كانت قدرته هكذا كيف يسوى في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusive address “You alone we worship” amounts to pure monotheism and the confession that there is no deity but God.
rows.anchor: قوله إياك نعبد يدل على أنه لا معبود إلا الله ومتى كان الأمر كذلك ثبت أنه لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among lower composite bodies, polytheists worship mineral idols of stone, gold, or silver, a particular tree, the calf, or humans claimed to be God's son, such as Ezra and Christ.
rows.anchor: يتخذون الأصنام إما من الأحجار أو من الذهب أو من الفضة ويعبدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Magians worship fire, which Rāzī classifies among simple lower bodies.
rows.anchor: الذين يعبدون النار وهم المجوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ṣābiʾa and most astrologers worship the sun, moon, and other stars and attribute fortune and misfortune to them.
rows.anchor: يعبدون الشمس والقمر وسائر الكواكب ويضيفون السعادة والنحوسة إليها

rows.speaker: المانوية والثنوية
rows.claim: Manichaeans and dualists posit Light and Darkness as the world's managers and partners with God.
rows.anchor: الذين قالوا مدبر العالم هو النور والظلمة وهؤلاء هم المانوية والثنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group treats angels as planetary spirits assigned to regions and kinds, fashions images of them, and worships those images.
rows.anchor: لكل إقليم روح معين من الأرواح الفلكية يدبره ولكل نوع من أنواع هذا العالم روح فلكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another group posits two sibling gods, one good and one evil, assigning worldly good to God and evil to Iblīs.
rows.anchor: الذين قالوا للعالم إلهان : أحدهما خير والآخر شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every polytheist worships a partner to seek benefit or escape harm, while strict monotheists place hope, fear, desire, and dread in God alone and worship and ask help only from Him.
rows.anchor: فكان رجاؤهم من الله وخوفهم من الله ورغبتهم في الله ورهبتهم من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding taxonomy concludes that “You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help” functions as the confession “There is no deity but God.”
rows.anchor: فكان قوله إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين قائما مقام قوله لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar remembrance combines glorification, praise, monotheism, divine greatness, and dependence; “praise belongs to God” already entails glorifying Him because only the perfect can perfect others.
rows.anchor: والشيء لا يكون مكملا متمما لغيره إلا إذا كان قبل ذلك تاما كاملا في ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah elaborates the five formulas of the familiar remembrance: praise establishes God's qualities, exclusive worship states monotheism, and asking His help expresses that no aim is fulfilled without Him.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن سورة الفاتحة من أولها إلى آخرها منطبقة على ذلك الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting “You” first identifies the true object of worship and produces reverent attention; Rāzī illustrates this with an expert wrestler who lost to a rustic until he recognized his opponent.
rows.anchor: قدم ذكر نفسه ليتنبه العابد على أن المعبود هو الله الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's greatness before undertaking difficult prayer makes its burdens easier, like taking strength before lifting weight or accepting pain for a beloved.
rows.anchor: فاذكر أولا قوله إياك نعبد لتذكرني وتحضر في قلبك معرفتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When satanic laziness or heedlessness arises, recalling God's presence restores insight and readiness for worship, as 7:201 describes the God-conscious remembering and seeing clearly.
rows.anchor: إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طيف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming God before the act prevents the devil from claiming the worship was directed to idols, celestial bodies, or another object; the order makes monotheism explicit.
rows.anchor: أما إذا غيرت هذا الترتيب وقلت أولا إياك ثم قلت ثانيا نعبد كان قولك أولا إياك صريحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the necessarily existent precedes contingent beings in existence, mention of the Eternal should precede all other speech.
rows.anchor: القديم الواجب لذاته متقدم في الوجود على المحدث الممكن لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discerning worshiper attends to the giver, not the gift, and in hardship to God, not the affliction; this keeps the heart absorbed in knowledge of God rather than worldly circumstances.
rows.anchor: من كان نظره في وقت النعمة إلى المنعم لا إلى النعمة كان نظره في وقت البلاء إلى المبتلي لا إلى البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant's continuing approach through supererogatory worship until God loves him illustrates the state of being absorbed in God's presence.
rows.anchor: لا يزال العبد يتقرب إلي بالنوافل حتى أحبه فإذا أحببته كنت له سمعا وبصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “we worship You” would not exclude worship of others, as polytheists do; saying “You alone we worship” clearly denies every rival.
rows.anchor: لو قيل نعبدك لم يفد نفي عبادتهم لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn of majesty portrays God's servants together as His subjects, whose service makes them rulers of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: أن هذه النون نون العظمة فكأنه قيل له متى كنت خارج الصلاة فلا تقل نحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “we worship” is humbler than “I worship”: it presents the speaker as one servant among God's servants rather than as a self-important individual.
rows.anchor: لو قال إياك أعبد لكان ذلك تكبرا ومعناه أني أنا العابد أما لما قال إياك نعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the same reasons might seem to favor putting God before “praise,” praise can be given to others, so “for God” must restrict it; worship can never go to another, so “You alone” comes first.
rows.anchor: الحمد لما جاز لغير الله في ظاهر الأمر كما جاز لله لا جرم حسن تقدم الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī asks whether the nūn in “we worship” is plural or divine majesty, since attributing greatness to oneself seems unfitting during humble worship; he says each answer has wisdom.
rows.anchor: النون في قوله نعبد إما أن تكون نون الجمع أو نون التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To explain the plural nūn, Rāzī cites a report that the first congregational takbīr is worth more than the world and all it contains.
rows.anchor: التكبيرة الأولى في صلاة الجماعة خير من الدنيا وما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great reward for congregational prayer does not justify harming Muslims with garlic or onion odor, much less by slander, backbiting, or denunciation.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان هذا الثواب لا يفي بذلك فكيف يفي بإيذاء المسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In congregational prayer “we” means the worshipers together; when praying alone it includes the worshiper and the angels who join him in worship.
rows.anchor: وإن كان يصلي وحده كان المراد أني أعبدك والملائكة معي في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural also includes all believers across east and west, so the worshiper seeks the welfare of fellow Muslims as well as his own.
rows.anchor: كان قد ذكر عبادة نفسه وعبادة جميع المؤمنين شرقا وغربا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet promises that God will fulfill all the needs of one who fulfills a Muslim's need.
rows.anchor: من قضى لمسلم حاجة قضى الله له جميع حاجاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the servant praises God through the whole opening sūrah, God raises his standing and asks him to care for all Muslims rather than only his own needs.
rows.anchor: فلا تقتصر على إصلاح مهماتك وحدك ولكن أصلح حوائج جميع المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because an individual's worship is mixed with shortcomings, he joins it to the worship of all worshipers; like a sale of ten slaves accepted all together or rejected all together, God may accept it with the worship of angels, prophets, and saints.
rows.anchor: فإما أن يرد الكل وهو غير جائز لأن قوله إياك نعبد دخل فيه عبادات الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing worship's benefits makes it sweet: it is human perfection, illuminates the heart, ennobles speech, beautifies the limbs, and brings the greatest happiness now and in the future.
rows.anchor: هذه الأحوال أشرف المراتب الإنسانية والدرجات البشرية فإذا كان حصول هذه الأحوال أعظم السعادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is a trust: fulfilling it is required and intrinsically excellent, and faithfulness in one direction brings God's faithfulness in return; 33:72 and 4:58 support the duty.
rows.anchor: أن العبادة أمانة بدليل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab leaves his camel outside, fulfills worship calmly, and asks God to return His trust; after the camel is stolen, its injured robber returns it, illustrating God's preservation of the worshiper's trust.
rows.anchor: إلهي أديت أمانتك فأين أمانتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says that the camel story illustrates a saying of the Prophet to Ibn ʿAbbās, whose wording follows in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وهو المراد من قوله عليه السلام لابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship transfers a person from the deceptive world and preoccupation with creatures into joy and the presence of God, bringing complete delight.
rows.anchor: الاشتغال بالعبادة انتقال من عالم الغرور إلى عالم السرور ومن الاشتغال بالخلق إلى حضرة الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī recounts that a snake fell near Abū Ḥanīfa during prayer, but he did not notice as people scattered.
rows.anchor: أن حية سقطت من السقف وتفرق الناس وكان أبو حنيفة في الصلاة ولم يشعر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr's diseased limb was amputated while he prayed, and he felt nothing.
rows.anchor: فلما شرع في الصلاة قطعوا منه ذلك العضو فلم يشعر عروة بذلك القطع

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet's chest made a rumbling sound like a boiling cauldron when he began prayer; Rāzī compares this absorption to women cutting their hands while captivated by Joseph's beauty.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان حين يشرع في الصلاة كانوا يسمعون من صدره أزيزا

rows.speaker: أهل التحقيق
rows.claim: The first rank worships for reward or to avoid punishment; Rāzī calls it very low because it treats God as a means to a worldly or created goal.
rows.anchor: أن يعبد الله طمعا في الثواب أو هربا من العقاب وهذا هو المسمى بالعبادة

rows.speaker: أهل التحقيق
rows.claim: The second rank worships to gain honor through service, accepted duties, or affiliation with God; it is higher but incomplete because its real aim remains something other than God.
rows.anchor: أن يعبد الله لأجل أن يتشرف بعبادته أو يتشرف بقبول تكاليفه

rows.speaker: أهل التحقيق
rows.claim: The highest rank worships God because He is God and Creator and the worshiper is His servant; this joins awe with humility, and intending prayer for God keeps it valid.
rows.anchor: أن يعبد الله لكونه إلها وخالقا ولكونه عبدا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship until death in 15:99 shows worship must never lapse and attests its rank; its four elements—glorification, praise, prostration, and worship—also ease sorrow by turning the heart from creatures to God.
rows.anchor: فأمر محمدا عليه الصلاة والسلام بالمواظبة على العبادة إلى أن يأتيه الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad God's servant at the supreme Ascension shows servitude's honor; some say it exceeds prophethood because it turns from creation to God, while prophethood turns back to people and their affairs.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن العبودية أشرف المقامات وإلا لما وصفه الله بهذه الصفة في أعلى مقامات المعراج

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some authorities rank servitude above prophethood because servitude turns from people toward God and withdraws from managing affairs, while a messenger turns from God toward people and manages their needs.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : العبودية أشرف من الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus first calls himself God's servant; that declaration vindicates his mother, brings good and averts harm, and precedes God's raising him, so sustained practical servitude deserves hope of Paradise.
rows.anchor: عيسى أول ما نطق قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God's oneness, God commands Moses to worship Him: monotheism is the root or tree, and servitude its branch or fruit; neither stands without the other.
rows.anchor: أمره بعد التوحيد بالعبودية ؛ لأن التوحيد أصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rationally, contingent beings receive existence and every perfection through God's creative power; thus every honor, joy, and virtue comes through servitude, the key to all good.
rows.anchor: فلما تعلقت قدرة الحق به وفاضت عليه آثار جوده وإيجاده حصل له الوجود وكمالات الوجود

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Rāzī introduces a saying from ʿAlī in which the following segment calls servanthood an honor and God’s lordship a distinction.
rows.anchor: وكان علي كرم الله وجهه يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual stations are knowledge of lordship and servitude; together they fulfill the covenant of 2:40. The opening praise establishes lordship, worship begins servitude, reliance completes it, and guidance is its fruit.
rows.anchor: وعند اجتماعهما يحصل العهد المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition from third person praise to direct address can be understood as God lifting the veil and drawing near after the worshiper has praised and acknowledged His attributes.
rows.anchor: حمدتني وأقررت بكوني إلها ربا رحمانا رحيما مالكا ليوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct address suits requests and service in God’s presence; the sūrah uses third person for praise and shifts to direct address for supplication, as prophets do.
rows.anchor: من أول السورة إلى قوله إياك نعبد ثناء والثناء في الغيبة أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī then quotes a prayer exalting servitude as honor and recognizing God as Lord.
rows.anchor: كفى بي فخرا أن أكون لك عبدا وكفى بي شرفا أن تكون لي ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī divides the case for reliance on God into rational proofs and transmitted evidence, then begins with the rational proofs.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه وجوه من العقل والنقل أما العقل فمن وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No act of obedience can be performed without God's protection from sin and enabling grace; Rāzī supports reliance on both rational and transmitted proofs.
rows.anchor: لا حول عن معصية الله إلا بعصمة الله ولا قوة على طاعة الله إلا بتوفيق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human capacity is equally disposed to acting or abstaining; action needs a preponderating motive, which cannot come from the servant without regress, so God must assist.
rows.anchor: فما لم يحصل المرجح لم يحصل الرجحان وذلك المرجح ليس من العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People with similar ability, intellect, effort, and desire seek true belief, yet only some attain it; the needed aid must come from God rather than a human or angel, which would restart the question.
rows.anchor: فوز البعض بدرك الحق لا يكون إلا بإعانة معين وما ذاك المعين إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may delay an act until a decisive motive enters the heart and opposing motives are removed; God creates these motives, which is the meaning of assistance.
rows.anchor: إلقاء تلك الداعية في القلب وإزالة الدواعي المعارضة لها ليست إلا من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الجبرية
rows.claim: The Jabriyya argue that if people acted independently, asking God for help with their actions would be pointless.
rows.anchor: لو كان العبد مستقلا بالفعل لما كان للاستعانة على الفعل فائدة

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: The Qadariyya argue that seeking assistance only makes sense if the servant can already perform the basic act; otherwise another's help is useless.
rows.anchor: الاستعانة إنما تحسن لو كان العبد متمكنا من أصل الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī resolves the dispute by saying capacity affects action only alongside a decisive motive; divine assistance creates that motive and removes the contrary one.
rows.anchor: القدرة لا تؤثر في الفعل إلا مع الداعية الجازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although assistance is usually sought before work begins, the worshiper asks God to help complete worship already begun and protect it from death, illness, or changed motives.
rows.anchor: شرعت في العبادة فأستعين بك في إتمامها فلا تمنعني من إتمامها بالموت ولا بالمرض

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying that the believer's heart lies between two fingers of the Merciful supports the worshiper's request for God to make his wandering heart present.
rows.anchor: قلب المؤمن بين أصبعين من أصابع الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshiper asks God alone, not Gabriel or Michael, following Abraham's refusal of Gabriel's offer while tied by Nimrod and his trust that God knows his state; Rāzī compares his own helplessness before Hell and God's promised rescue.
rows.anchor: فقال : أما إليك فلا فقال : سله فقال : حسبي من سؤالي علمه بحالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Help from any intermediary itself depends on God's help, so the worshiper should cut out that intermediary and ask God directly.
rows.anchor: فإذا كانت إعانة الغير لا تتم إلا بإعانتك فلنقطع هذه الواسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following worship with a request for help prevents pride: the rank achieved through worship came from God's support, not the servant's own strength.
rows.anchor: المقصود من ذكر قوله وإياك نستعين إزالة العجب وإفناء تلك النخوة والكبر

none: Bare chapter heading introducing the explanation of 1:6.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent paradox is that a believer already has guidance; Rāzī answers that asking for the straight path can mean seeking the earlier believers' strength in bearing hardship for God.
rows.anchor: المراد منه صراط الأولين في تحمل المشاق العظيمة لأجل مرضاة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was beaten repeatedly and each time prayed for his people to be guided; Muhammad's repeated daily recitation of al-Fātiḥah means he uttered the request more often, so Noah's single prayer does not make him superior.
rows.anchor: وكان يقول في كل مرة : اللهم اهد قومي فإنهم لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance also means the just middle between excess and neglect in every character and action, including desire, anger, and spending; even a believer needs this balance.
rows.anchor: وهما مذمومان والحق هو الوسط ويتأكد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer may know God through one proof yet overlook the many signs in created things; guidance asks God to reveal how each thing evidences His essence, attributes, power, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: عرف الله بدليل واحد فلا موجود من أقسام الممكنات إلا وفيه دلائل على وجود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is wholehearted turning to God, as 42:52–53 and 6:153 say; it means following the prophets' endurance in sacrifice, obedience, exile, and even death, while the verse also offers the easier hope of repentance and accepted mercy.
rows.anchor: وذلك الصراط المستقيم هو أن يكون الإنسان معرضا عما سوى الله مقبلا بكلية قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker faces pressure from friends, enemies, Satan, passions, sectarian extremes, weak reason, short life, risky experience, and difficult destiny; he asks for a smooth path out to Paradise.
rows.anchor: كثرة الأحباب يجرونني إلى طريق والأعداء إلى طريق ثان والشيطان إلى طريق ثالث

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the straight path as Islam, while others say it is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: الصراط المستقيم : الإسلام وقال بعضهم : القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects those identifications because the following apposition points to the path of earlier nations, who did not have the Qur'an and Islam; the intended path is that of the truthful and Paradise-worthy.
rows.anchor: بدل من الصراط المستقيم وإذا كان كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Path” rather than the synonyms way or road evokes the path to Hell, increasing fear and caution.
rows.anchor: لفظ الصراط مذكرا لصراط جهنم ؛ فيكون الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation of “guide us” is “keep us firm in the guidance You have given,” as in 3:8; even learned people can be misled by a subtle doubt.
rows.anchor: ثبتنا على الهداية التي وهبتها منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural prayer is more likely to be answered: if any Muslim merits a response, God's generosity will not answer some worshipers and reject the rest.
rows.anchor: إذا أجاب الله الدعاء في البعض فهو أكرم من أن يرده في الباقي

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says to call on God with tongues not used in sin; when the Companions ask who has such tongues, he tells them to pray for one another because none sinned with another's tongue.
rows.anchor: ادعوا الله بألسنة ما عصيتموه بها قالوا : يا رسول الله ومن لنا بتلك الألسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier wording “praise belongs to God,” rather than “I praise God,” includes all worshipers; the servant similarly says “guide us” to include them in his request.
rows.anchor: ألست قلت في أول السورة الحمد لله وما قلت أحمد الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that congregation is mercy and separation punishment; the servant therefore speaks collectively in praise, worship, reliance, guidance, following the righteous, and avoiding the condemned and astray, hoping to remain with the righteous in the next life.
rows.anchor: الجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب فلما أردت تحميدك ذكرت حمد الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Geometry defines a straight line as the shortest distance between two points; a weak servant asks for this shorter route.
rows.anchor: الخط المستقيم هو أقصر خط يصل بين نقطتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A straight road is uniquely recognizable, while crooked paths resemble and confuse one another, making the straight way safer.
rows.anchor: المستقيم فلا يشابهه غيره فكان أبعد عن الخوف والآفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight route reaches the goal, whereas a crooked route does not.
rows.anchor: الطريق المستقيم يوصل إلى المقصود والمعوج لا يوصل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight route remains stable, whereas crooked paths change; this is the fourth reason to ask for it.
rows.anchor: المستقيم لا يتغير والمعوج يتغير

none: Bare chapter heading introducing the explanation of 1:7.
